- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially after sharp price spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5%.
- Underestimate in the final 5–10 days of the forecast; adjust upward by 1–3% to align with recent mean reversion trends.
- If model shows a sustained upward trend after a spike, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% to avoid over-optimism.
- When true outcome is consistently lower than forecast, especially in the middle of the horizon, apply a downward bias correction of 1–3% per day.
- If forecast is consistently higher than true outcome across all days, apply a global offset correction of -1.5 to -3.0 units to reduce overall overestimation.
- Avoid forecasting based on recent high volatility; use 30-day moving average as a baseline for smoothing out erratic spikes.
